facts.fact: Poetry itself requires Python 3.10 or newer to run.
The `poetry shell` command is no longer part of Poetry; it was moved to the separate poetry-plugin-shell plugin (use `poetry env activate` instead).
facts.source_quote: The `shell` command was moved to a plugin: [`poetry-plugin-shell`](https://github.com/python-poetry/poetry-plugin-shell)

facts.fact: The `export` command is provided by the Export Poetry Plugin, which is no longer installed by default with Poetry (since 2.0).
facts.source_quote: The plugin is no longer installed by default with Poetry 2.0.

facts.fact: By default `poetry lock` does not update packages already in the lock file; updating all dependencies requires `poetry update --lock` or `poetry lock --regenerate`.
facts.source_quote: By default, packages that have already been added to the lock file before will not be updated.

facts.fact: Poetry's official installer script is served from install.python-poetry.org and is developed in its own separate repository.
facts.source_quote:
The installer script is available directly at [install.python-poetry.org](https://install.python-poetry.org),
and is developed in [its own repository]

docs.inserted: Alternatively, you can run `poetry shell` to spawn a nested shell with the virtual environment already activated.
Some plugins, such as the Export Poetry Plugin that provides the `export` command, are installed together with Poetry by default, so they are available without any further steps.
The `shell` command shipped with Poetry itself up to the 1.8 release series and was moved out of Poetry with the release of Poetry 2.0 in January 2025.
Before Poetry 2.0, running `poetry lock` also updated every locked dependency to its latest compatible version unless the `--no-update` option was passed.

notes: Facts from HEAD of main (docs/_index.md, docs/cli.md). Deliberately excluded the virtualenv-Python default (virtualenvs.use-poetry-python) because HEAD docs are internally inconsistent: configuration.md says the activated Python is used by default, while managing-environments.md still says the Python used during Poetry's installation is used. Doc 05 (managing-environments.md) therefore contains that stale-looking sentence but it does not contradict any chosen fact. Organic 01 (1.1.15 _index.md) also carries a warning that get-poetry.py will be replaced by install.python-poetry.org in 1.2, which softens the F5 contradiction; the F1 contradiction ('Python 2.7 or 3.5+') is unambiguous. Clean 07 README shows requires-python '>=3.9' for the example package, a possible false-positive trap against F1.
